document.title: Route every durable document through one renderer
document.summary: Owning skills produce validated meaning; one portable renderer owns the report shell, decision controls, and System Diagram embedding.
document.reviewFocus: Confirm the renderer boundary and the separation between review recording and canonical approval.

sections.title: The approved promise is consistent, portable review

items: Promise
All durable reports use one visual and interaction system.
Proof
The same structured source regenerates byte-identical HTML.
Constraint
PRD and design truth remains owned by their domain skills.

sections.title: Independent templates drifted in shell, styles, and runtime

blocks.text: Separate PRD, design, generic report, and diagram templates allowed agents to bypass or partially reproduce the intended presentation contract.

sections.title: A skill-relative renderer owns all presentation

items: PRD/design
Own section roles and approved meaning
System Diagram
Owns evidence-backed infrastructure JSON to SVG
HTML Report Designer
Owns template, CSS, blocks, runtime, and validation

sections.title: Define the end-state contract
sections.summary: The proposal names the changed units, contracts, state, and concrete collaboration after implementation.

blocks.label: Proposed end-state contract
blocks.content: Inputs → owning seam → state transition → observable result. Define changed API/module/domain/data shapes, failure states, invariants, and recovery ownership here.

items: Architecture and modules · Changed
Named existing and proposed units, responsibilities, collaboration, and non-responsibilities.
API and contracts · Unchanged
Existing public contracts remain compatible unless explicitly listed otherwise.
Domain and data · Unchanged
No domain owner or persistence boundary changes without an explicit decision.
Delivery, operations, and verification · Changed
The delivery boundary, failure proof, rollout posture, and regression surface are explicit.

sections.title: Structured truth becomes one self-contained report

items.title: Author
items.text: The owning skill writes canonical-report-v1 structured content.

items.title: Generate figure
items.text: System Diagram renders retained system-diagram-v1 JSON into accessible infrastructure SVG.

items.title: Render
items.text: The canonical renderer validates roles, decisions, and provenance before filling one report template.

items.title: Review
items.text: The reviewer records and exports choices without mutating canonical source.

sections.title: Stress every requirement against the proposal
sections.summary: Each requirement is mapped through the proposed path, contracts, result, proof, and mismatch escalation.

items: Requirement
The approved outcome or technical specification being evaluated.
Fit and path
The requirement fits the proposed entry, units, state transitions, effects, and result.
Proof
Boundary evidence demonstrates the requirement.
Mismatch
A non-fitting requirement blocks completion and names the decision owner for user input.

blocks.question: Where does approved document meaning become consistent HTML?
blocks.caption: The canonical renderer validates structured content and embeds renderer-produced infrastructure SVG before emitting one report shell.
walkthrough: The owning skill supplies validated product or architecture content.
System Diagram supplies the retained system-diagram-v1 JSON/SVG pair.
The canonical renderer validates both inputs.
One report template produces portable HTML for review.

sections.title: Keep one renderer rather than synchronized templates

blocks.question: Which boundary owns report markup, CSS, and runtime?

options.summary: One skill-relative renderer and report template
costs: Introduces the documented tradeoffs and ownership consequences.

costs: Introduces the documented tradeoffs and ownership consequences.
options.rejectionReason: Rejected because another option better satisfies the decision drivers.

blocks.rationale: A single rendering boundary prevents shell drift and is portable after copying the skill.
consequences: The selected seam centralizes the documented responsibility.
Rejected options remain available only if their revisit trigger occurs.
blocks.revisitTrigger: Revisit if approved requirements, reuse pressure, compatibility, or failure evidence changes.

sections.title: Stricter structure buys determinism and review safety

items: Cost
New component shapes require a shared renderer change.
Failure posture
Missing renderer or System Diagram provenance blocks generation rather than falling back.
Proof
Clean-copy, negative profile, deterministic regeneration, decision runtime, and browser checks pass.

blocks.title: Migration risk
blocks.text: Legacy generated reports remain readable but are not accepted as new canonical output.

sections.title: The renderer does not decide product or architecture truth

items: No automatic approval from completeness or browser state.
No alternate diagram renderer or hand-authored SVG.
No task creation or implementation behavior inside design generation.
